I got to help destroy an old dam in the Columbia River Gorge! I worked with the forestry department (A scout master worked for them) and we hauled the debris by hand down the trails. It was a lot of fun and we helped restore spawning grounds for Giant Pacific Salamanders and Salmon.

I had about 15 other scouts show up to help and 10 adults, some forestry workers others dads. It took about 7 hours of actual labor and most of that was hauling. I have no idea how long the planning took in total. it was months in the making.

I took my kid their since we live nearby and actually got to see smolt (teeny salmon babies) which almost made me cry. It is a cool connection I have to a forest I grew up in.

ELI5: Why do stars blink in the sky, but planets don't?

Because of our atmosphere (the part protecting us from harmful stuff from space) that refracts light causing stars to appear 'twinkling'.

Stars emit their own light while planets don't. Light we see from planets are from multiple sources (like multiple flash lights bouncing off a disco ball) and they are also more closer to us than stars (stars appear as like a dot while planets appear like a disk).

You can read more into it here or just its accompanying video.

Imagine the stars being like showers. If you are very close the the star, you'll be hit by the water all the time. If the star is far away, you'll only be hit by the water every now and then. The light emitted from the stars spreads out over distance, and the light will not always be hitting you.

Planets on the other hand, are much smaller, and the ones you see, are so close that the light that bounces off them will more often be visible.
